title: #19 Oddbjørn Dybvad: Investing in Value Creators

reader_summary.headline: Welcome to Investing by the Books, a podcast by Radai.
reader_summary.overview: Welcome to Investing by the Books, a podcast by Radai. I'm your host, Eddie Panyan, and next to me here in the studio is my friend Niklas Savos. Spring is approaching, sun is shining, and we have a really interesting guest today.

key_points.text: Today we are talking with Odbjohn Duvad, investment director and portfolio manager of REQ Global Compounders.
key_points.evidence_quote: Today we are talking with Odbjohn Duvad, investment director and portfolio manager of REQ Global Compounders.

key_points.text: He is also the author of Investing in Value Creators, time-tested principles for long-term stock investments.
key_points.evidence_quote: He is also the author of Investing in Value Creators, time-tested principles for long-term stock investments.

key_points.text: To me, what really stands out with this book is Odbjern's innovative conclusions from his long experience as a money manager.
key_points.evidence_quote: To me, what really stands out with this book is Odbjern's innovative conclusions from his long experience as a money manager.

key_points.text: He also illustrates his thoughts very well through both tables and graphs.
key_points.evidence_quote: He also illustrates his thoughts very well through both tables and graphs, and he touches upon both qualitative factors such as corporate culture and management, but also a lot of quantitative factors, which are, yeah, the most important ones in his philosophy.

thesis: The guest argues that investment analysis relies on pattern recognition and that the philosophy centers on investing in 'value creators'—companies capable of deploying capital at high returns over long periods. This approach focuses on three essential ingredients: capital allocation by outstanding management teams, decentralization, and people, with a specific emphasis on finding teams that have the freedom to reinvest capital organically and through acquisitions.
